sampling_model.design: Observational independent sampling from one support-closed compact restricted additive-noise law \(P\).
sampling_model.units: The units \(V^{(1)},\ldots,V^{(n)}\) are independent draws of all \(d\) labelled nodes.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment; the causal target is the labelled DAG \(G_0\).
sampling_model.overlap: Innovation densities are strictly positive on relative interiors, conditional-support fibers are connected, feasible structural outputs stay inside the declared node intervals, and node variances are bounded away from zero.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cross-fitted local-polynomial regression estimates conditional means; held-out squared losses estimate risks, bounded continuous characteristic kernels estimate residual HSIC, and a separate residual-coordinate Lipschitz premise controls plug-in residual perturbations.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Li et al. implement Equation (6) with learned neural-network regressions and residual-independence test p-values, and Theorem 4.3 assumes a global strict fitness ranking whenever two orders have different ancestral-reversal counts before concluding recovery under that premise.
The terminal-node normalized explained variance in a random linear causal chain converges to one under a positive mean log-edge-weight condition.
A causally minimal restricted additive-noise model satisfying the Condition 19 configuration requirement has a DAG identifiable from its observational distribution.
Greedy sparsest-permutation algorithms are pointwise consistent under faithfulness through weakly decreasing covered-arrow walks.
Sample splitting gives a fitted-residual dHSIC statistic the same asymptotic null distribution as its exact-residual counterpart.
Studentized cross-HSIC converges to a standard normal law under fixed bounded-kernel null distributions satisfying a second-moment condition.
A likelihood order estimator is consistent when the minimum wrong-order log-residual-variance gap is positive.

body.tldr: For the exact \(\alpha=1\) population-oracle analogue of GENE Equation (6), a primitive edgewise inequality on support-closed matching-component additive-noise models forces a positive reversal-correcting insertion at every wrong order, so best improvement and independence pruning recover the labelled DAG with a finite oracle-query budget. This is a certified success region, not a theorem for Li et al.'s full nonlinear class. For every \(\eta\in(0,1/2)\), an explicitly parameterized relatively open bivariate family, including a nonempty relatively open non-affine subfamily, makes the identifiable causal model \(X\to Y\) have the wrong order as its unique global and hence insertion-local maximizer with score advantage strictly greater than \(\eta\); the universal sharp supremum is \(1/2\). Cross-fitted simultaneous bands abstain at unresolved independence labels; on separated labels, \(w_S\le4d w_R/\underline v\), and direct margin inequalities yield the sufficient sample size \(n\gtrsim\log(M_d/\alpha)\max\{(d/\delta_{\mathrm{pair}})^{\max\{2,(d+5)/6\}},\lambda^{-(d+5)/3}\}\), with the score-margin elbow at \(d=7\) and no minimax claim. Under \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(d)\) and the stated HSIC separation promise, the set-valued output covers \(G_0\) with probability at least \(1-\alpha\) even when the width inequalities fail; those inequalities are required only for singleton recovery, and otherwise the compatible-DAG union may be singleton or multiple.

project_justification.gap: Li et al. (2025, Equation (6)) use finite-sample neural-network fits and residual-independence p-values, while their Theorem 4.3 assumes a global score ranking across orders with different ancestral-reversal counts. Peters et al. (2014) identify restricted additive-noise models through Condition 19 configurations, but observational identifiability alone supplies neither local ascent nor protection against a wrong population-score optimum. Existing work also does not provide simultaneous learned-risk and residual-HSIC uncertainty propagation for adaptive GENE search.
project_justification.niche: The useful boundary has three auditable pieces: a structural success certificate with finite population-query complexity, a genuinely open set of identifiable mechanisms on which the exact population score fails as sharply as its range permits, and finite-sample confidence logic that returns a singleton only when navigation and pruning margins are resolved.
project_justification.fill: On the matching-component subclass, the forward-versus-reverse edge signal inequality gives a strict correcting-gain bound and labelled-DAG oracle recovery. A six-node nonlinear witness separates this certificate from Li et al.'s global ranking premise, while a rare-component bivariate construction and its non-affine perturbations produce, for every \(\eta<1/2\), an open trapped-order family with advantage at least \(\eta\). Simultaneous bands yield \(w_S\le K_d w_R\), explicit margin conditions, the \(d=7\) score-rate elbow, and set-valued abstention near independence.

body.related_work: Li et al. (2025, Equation (6), Definition 4.1, and Theorem 4.3 with its proof on page 5) define the released finite-sample score using neural-network prediction and residual-independence test p-values and prove greedy recovery under a global reversal-monotone fitness premise. The present score is its exact \(\alpha=1\) population-oracle analogue. The matching-class navigation theorem is therefore not transferred to their full nonlinear class. The included nonlinear separation and trapped-order witnesses are nevertheless members of that broader class and hence transfer only as existential examples; the trap violates the premise needed by Theorem 4.3 and does not refute that conditional theorem. Peters et al. (2014, Condition 19, Definition 27, and Theorem 28 on pages 13--16) prove identification under their positive-density restricted-ANM configuration requirement. Their Proposition 17 gives a pointwise nonconstancy characterization of causal minimality, whereas the compact-support model here uses positive-parent-law-measure nonconstancy and a separate relative-interior identification bridge. Reisach et al. (2023, Sections 3 and 5) analyze scale-normalized explained variance, informing the primitive ratios but not the GENE insertion landscape. Solus, Wang, and Uhler (2021, Proposition 8 and Theorem 9) study covered-arrow walks for a sparsity score rather than GENE insertion ascent. Pfister et al. (2018, Theorem E.2 and Proposition E.3) and Shekhar, Kim, and Ramdas (2023, Theorems 6 and 7) provide kernel-independence and sample-splitting ingredients but not simultaneous adaptive graph sets with learned normalized risks. Buhlmann, Peters, and Ernest (2014, Theorems 1 and 2) analyze likelihood order estimation and pruning under a different wrong-order variance margin.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The success certificate is sufficient only on matching-component DAGs and is not an observable necessary-and-sufficient boundary for general GENE landscapes. The sharp bivariate construction proves a margin-indexed relatively open failure region, including a relatively open non-affine subfamily, inside the identifiable nonlinear-ANM class and attains the universal one-half supremum only as a limit; it does not classify the intervening general class. Exact independence remains discontinuous: the population trap handles it pointwise by support geometry throughout its open structural family, while finite-sample inference requires the stated HSIC separation promise and otherwise retains both labels. Under the matching class and that separation promise, simultaneous coverage still gives \(\mathbb P\{G_0\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_n\}\ge1-\alpha\) when the score and HSIC width inequalities fail, but only the width inequalities certify singleton recovery; the compatible-DAG union may then be singleton or multiple. The residual-estimation contribution to the HSIC radius uses the stated nonstandard residual-coordinate Lipschitz premise. The displayed sample-size order suppresses fixed regularity constants and is sufficient, not minimax optimal.
body.honest_scope: The delivered population results are a compact-support identification bridge, a matching-subclass insertion-navigation theorem, a six-node strict separation witness, finite-query oracle recovery, a quadratic positive-gain witness, and, for every \(\eta\in(0,1/2)\), a sharp relatively open bivariate trapped-order family with a nonempty relatively open non-affine subfamily. The wrong order is the unique global and hence insertion-local maximizer by more than \(\eta\), while the universal supremum of this score advantage is \(1/2\). The matching-subclass theorem does not establish success on Li et al.'s full nonlinear class; the nonlinear witnesses transfer to that class only existentially, and the trap does not contradict Theorem 4.3 because its global-ranking premise fails there. The simultaneous-band theorem gives \(w_S\le4d w_R/\underline v\) on separated labels when \(w_R<\underline v/2\), together with direct sufficient conditions \(K_1d\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{6/(d+5)}\}<\delta_{\mathrm{pair}}\) and \(K_2\{t_n^{1/2}+t_n^{3/(d+5)}\}<\lambda\), where \(t_n=\log(M_d/\alpha)/n\), and the \(d=7\) score-rate elbow. Under \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pair}}(d)\) and the existing HSIC separation promise, \(\mathbb P\{G_0\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_n\}\ge1-\alpha\) remains valid even when those width inequalities fail; singleton recovery requires the inequalities, and otherwise the compatible-DAG union may be singleton or multiple. No minimax rate, observable general-class boundary, or claim against Li et al. Theorem 4.3 is made. The released Sachs workflow remains an audit case: a fixed chi-square threshold does not certify a population margin, and intervention-informed reference directions do not follow from an observational acyclic ANM alone.
